headline: No direct interaction risk: both agents are docs-only, non-runnable, and expose no shared write or network surfaces; remaining concerns are limited to inferred workflow coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. Agent A is an awesome-list repo with no I/O surfaces, and agent B has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, filesystem, or browser surfaces enabled. Without a shared channel, A cannot inject instructions into B.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, stdin/stdout bridge, or MCP server is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other agent's raw text as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared copy/paste channels.
Disable any future MCP bridge unless provenance filtering is added.
Review any orchestrator wiring before enabling cross-agent message passing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data-leakage pathway is evident. Agent A touches no data classes and has network_egress none; agent B also has network_egress none and no filesystem reads or writes. With no shared workspace or outbound transport, there is no documented route for sensitive data to flow between them.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem access to a shared workspace, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent gains outbound API access, data exfiltration risk changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents offline from external networks.
Avoid mounting any shared workspace containing sensitive files.
Recheck permissions before enabling file ingestion or export.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability conflict is blocked by the profiles. Agent A has no write, shell, or git capabilities exposed, while agent B explicitly cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. Since neither can mutate shared resources, there is no write-write conflict to manage.
conditions: IF agent A is given write or git permissions in the same directory as agent B, conflict risk must be reassessed.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, locking requirements change.
mitigations: Keep agent A read-only in the current deployment.
Do not grant agent B filesystem or git write permissions.
If shared state is introduced, add explicit locking before use.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error pathway is not supported by the profiles. Agent A is a non-runnable reference list, not an action-producing model, and agent B has no downstream action surfaces such as shell, email, or API calls. There is no documented chain where B would execute A's outputs as authoritative actions.
conditions: IF agent A is replaced with a generator of operational facts and agent B is given action-taking tools, cascading-error risk becomes plausible.
IF B begins treating A's text as authoritative without verification, reassess.
mitigations: Keep A as a static reference source only.
Require human review before any downstream action.
Do not add action-taking tools to B without validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and touch no data classes; neither profile states residency, retention, or regulated-data handling. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are absent, there is no documented residency or retention violation to assess.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data classes, compliance controls must be re-evaluated.
IF residency or retention policies are introduced, compare them before deployment.
mitigations: Document data classes before onboarding either agent.
Add retention and residency policies if regulated data is introduced.
Review compliance requirements before connecting the agents to production data.
